prompt:
# Subject Merge Fine Clustering

## Quick Start

Inside one topic area, create tight candidate clusters that are worth a later same-concept decision. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Identity Filter

Cluster candidates only when they might be the same teachable idea at the same level, testable with the same question.

Do not cluster just because candidates share a keyword. Keep candidates separate when one adds implementation, math, limitation, application, deeper mechanism, tool-specific behavior, or a broader/narrower student action.

Doubt means singleton. Under-clustering is safer than sending unrelated candidates to merge evaluation.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short candidate cluster",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may share concept identity.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- Each non-singleton cluster has a plausible same-concept reason.
- Implementation, limitation, application, math, and deeper-revisit candidates were not grouped with definitions just because labels overlap.
- Mixed-language same-level candidates were clustered when their teachable idea matches.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

area.label: Word Embeddings Concepts
area.rationale: Core embedding ideas: distributional hypothesis, analogy, cosine similarity, Word2Vec architectures, training, negative sampling, GloVe, fastText, contextual embeddings (ELMo, BERT).

candidates.label: Analogias com Vetores de Palavras (Word2Vec)
candidates.description: Word2Vec produz embeddings densos que permitem realizar analogias através de operações aritméticas, como 'rei - homem + mulher ≈ rainha', evidenciando que as relações semânticas são codificadas como direções no espaço vetorial.
coverage_criteria: Explique como vetores word2vec podem ser usados para resolver analogias.
Forneça um exemplo de analogia usando operações com vetores.

candidates.label: Incorporação 2D Simplificada para Visualizar Similaridade
candidates.description: É possível construir word embeddings bidimensionais atribuindo manualmente pontuações (ex.: fofura e tamanho) para animais, de modo que palavras similares fiquem próximas no espaço vetorial, ilustrando o princípio da similaridade semântica por proximidade espacial.
coverage_criteria: Dado um plot 2D de animais com escores de atributos, identifique os mais similares.
Explique como a distância euclidiana mede similaridade em um embedding 2D.

candidates.label: Alta Dimensionalidade dos Embeddings Reais e Redução de Dimensionalidade
candidates.description: Modelos word2vec reais usam centenas de dimensões (100-300) para capturar relações semânticas complexas, impossibilitando visualização direta; técnicas como t-SNE ou PCA são necessárias para projetar em 2D.
coverage_criteria: Explique por que embeddings reais são de alta dimensionalidade.
Cite uma técnica para visualizar embeddings de alta dimensionalidade.

candidates.label: Hipótese Distributiva
candidates.description: A hipótese distributiva afirma que palavras que aparecem em contextos similares tendem a ter significados similares, fundamentando a representação vetorial semântica.
coverage_criteria: Enuncie a hipótese distributiva.
Explique como essa hipótese justifica o uso de word embeddings.

candidates.label: Similaridade por Cosseno entre Vetores de Palavras
candidates.description: A similaridade de cosseno mede o ângulo entre dois vetores para quantificar proximidade semântica, sendo preferida ao produto escalar por normalizar a magnitude e evitar viés de palavras frequentes.
coverage_criteria: Defina similaridade de cosseno.
Explique por que é preferida ao produto escalar para comparar vetores de palavras.

candidates.label: Arquiteturas do Word2Vec: CBOW e Skip-Gram
candidates.description: Word2Vec possui duas arquiteturas principais: CBOW (Continuous Bag-of-Words) prevê a palavra central a partir do contexto, enquanto Skip-Gram prevê o contexto a partir da palavra central.
coverage_criteria: Diferencie CBOW de Skip-Gram.
Descreva a entrada e saída de cada arquitetura.

candidates.label: Treinamento do Word2Vec e Amostragem Negativa
candidates.description: O treinamento do Word2Vec maximiza a probabilidade de pares palavra-contexto usando uma função softmax; para reduzir custo, a amostragem negativa gera exemplos negativos, otimizando o cálculo.
coverage_criteria: Explique o objetivo de treinamento do Word2Vec.
Qual o propósito da amostragem negativa?

candidates.label: Comparação entre Word2Vec, GloVe e fastText
candidates.description: Word2Vec foca em contexto local, GloVe utiliza estatísticas globais de co-ocorrência, e fastText usa subword n-grams para representar palavras desconhecidas, oferecendo diferentes trade-offs.
coverage_criteria: Compare Word2Vec, GloVe e fastText em termos de contexto e tratamento de palavras desconhecidas.

candidates.label: BERT: Embeddings Bidirecionais com Transformers
candidates.description: BERT é um modelo de embedding contextual que utiliza transformers bidirecionais para considerar o contexto à esquerda e à direita, gerando representações dinâmicas e ricas.
coverage_criteria: Descreva a principal característica do BERT em relação a modelos unidirecionais.

candidates.label: Word Embeddings: Definição e Motivação
candidates.description: Word embeddings são representações densas de palavras em um espaço vetorial, capturando significado semântico e contrastando com representações esparsas como bag-of-words.
coverage_criteria: Explique o que são word embeddings.
Como eles se diferenciam de representações esparsas?

candidates.label: Distributional Hypothesis of Meaning
candidates.description: The distributional hypothesis states that words with similar meanings occur in similar contexts. This concept covers the idea that a word's meaning can be inferred from the company it keeps, demonstrated through contextual inference examples.
coverage_criteria: State the distributional hypothesis.
Given example sentences, identify words that are likely semantically related based on shared contexts.
Explain why antonyms like 'hot' and 'cold' can be considered similar under this hypothesis.

candidates.label: Word Vectors as Numerical Representations
candidates.description: Words can be encoded as vectors of numbers, where each dimension represents a semantic or descriptive feature such as authority, richness, or gender. This concept forms the basis for representing text data in a continuous vector space.
coverage_criteria: Explain that a word vector is a numerical encoding of a word's features.
Provide examples of possible features for a given word (e.g., 'king' could have high authority, male, royalty).
Distinguish between hand-crafted features and automatically learned features.

candidates.label: Vector Arithmetic for Semantic Analogies
candidates.description: Word vectors learned by Word2Vec support vector arithmetic that reflects semantic relationships, enabling analogy solving (e.g., 'king' - 'man' + 'woman' ≈ 'queen').
coverage_criteria: Given a word vector equation, predict the expected result word for a simple analogy.
Explain that vector difference can capture the relationship between two words.
Perform vector addition or subtraction to solve an analogy task.

candidates.label: Semantic and Syntactic Relationships in Word2Vec Embeddings
candidates.description: Word2Vec embeddings capture a variety of linguistic relationships, including verb tenses, capital-country associations, and gender pairs, by encoding them as consistent vector offsets.
coverage_criteria: Provide at least two distinct types of linguistic relationships that word vectors can capture (e.g., tense, geography).
Explain why such relationships emerge from the training objective.

candidates.label: Similarity Measures for Word Vectors
candidates.description: Euclidean distance and cosine similarity are two metrics used to quantify the similarity between word vectors. Euclidean distance measures straight-line distance in vector space, while cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors, often preferred in high-dimensional spaces.
coverage_criteria: Calculate Euclidean distance between two vectors.
Compute cosine similarity between two vectors.
Explain the differences between Euclidean distance and cosine similarity and when each might be more appropriate.

candidates.label: Word Embeddings as Neural Network Weights
candidates.description: In Word2Vec, the word embeddings are the learned weights connecting the one-hot input to the hidden layer (or hidden to output, depending on architecture).
coverage_criteria: Indicate that after training, the embedding for a word is extracted from the weight matrix of the neural network.

candidates.label: Count-based Word Vector Construction and Dimensionality Reduction
candidates.description: Word vectors can be built by counting word co-occurrences in contexts from a corpus. This yields high-dimensional vectors that often contain redundant information; dimensionality reduction techniques like SVD compress them into a smaller, more manageable number of dimensions (e.g., 100-300).
coverage_criteria: Construct a simple co-occurrence matrix from a small corpus.
Explain why raw co-occurrence vectors can be too high-dimensional.
Name dimensionality reduction as a solution and state typical reduced dimensions.

candidates.label: Word Embedding
candidates.description: Dense, low-dimensional vector representations of words that capture semantic similarities, enabling analogies through vector arithmetic.
coverage_criteria: Explain how word embeddings capture meaning (e.g., similar words have close vectors).
Give an example of an analogy solvable with embeddings.
Contrast word embeddings with one-hot encoding.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Word2Vec
candidates.description: A shallow neural network model that learns word embeddings from large corpora using either the Continuous Bag of Words (CBOW) or skip-gram architecture.
coverage_criteria: Distinguish between CBOW and skip-gram training objectives.
Explain how Word2Vec produces dense vectors for words.
Describe a practical use of pre-trained Word2Vec embeddings.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
candidates.description: GloVe is an unsupervised learning algorithm for generating word embeddings by factorizing a word co-occurrence matrix, capturing global statistical information.
coverage_criteria: Explain how GloVe uses a co-occurrence matrix to learn word embeddings.
Compare GloVe's approach to Word2Vec's context-window method.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Semantic Similarity and Properties of Embedding Space
candidates.description: In a distributional framework, words are similar if they share similar contexts. Embedding vectors place these words in a space where distance (e.g., cosine) reflects similarity. Well‑trained embeddings also exhibit clustering of related words and support analogical reasoning (e.g., king - man + woman ≈ queen).
coverage_criteria: Explain how word similarity is defined by context rather than spelling.
Given a 2D plot, identify which words are most similar based on distance.
Describe the analogy property of ideal embeddings with an example.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Training a Custom Embedding Layer
candidates.description: A neural network can include an embedding layer initialized randomly and trained end‑to‑end for a specific task, producing specialized word representations. This requires large amounts of data.
coverage_criteria: Describe how a custom embedding layer is trained within a model.
State one advantage and one disadvantage of training embeddings from scratch.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Word2vec: CBOW and Skip‑gram Architectures
candidates.description: Word2vec learns embeddings by training a shallow neural network on a prediction task: Continuous Bag‑of‑Words (CBOW) predicts a target word from context, while Skip‑gram predicts context words from a target word.
coverage_criteria: Differentiate CBOW and Skip‑gram and state what each predicts.
Explain how Word2vec creates dense word vectors from unlabeled text.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
candidates.description: GloVe improves on Word2vec by leveraging a word co‑occurrence matrix, training vectors such that their dot product approximates the log of co‑occurrence probability, thereby incorporating global corpus statistics.
coverage_criteria: Explain how GloVe differs from Word2vec regarding global information.
Describe the role of the co‑occurrence matrix in GloVe.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: fastText: Subword Embeddings
candidates.description: fastText represents each word as the sum of its character n‑gram embeddings, allowing it to build vectors for out‑of‑vocabulary words and handle morphologically rich languages.
coverage_criteria: Explain how fastText’s subword approach addresses the out‑of‑vocabulary problem.
Describe the difference between Word2vec and fastText regarding word representation.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: ELMo: Contextualized Word Embeddings
candidates.description: ELMo uses a bidirectional LSTM to produce word vectors that depend on the entire input sentence, allowing the same word to have different representations in different contexts (e.g., homonyms).
coverage_criteria: Explain why ELMo provides different embeddings for the same word in different sentences.
Describe the advantage of context‑dependent over static word embeddings.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Using Pre‑trained Word Embeddings
candidates.description: Pre‑trained word vectors can be used in two ways: as static features (fixed during downstream training) or fine‑tuned (adjusted to the task). The Gensim library provides convenient access to pre‑trained models (Word2vec, GloVe, fastText) and similarity operations.
coverage_criteria: List and describe the two modes of using pre‑trained embeddings.
Write code to load a pre‑trained model from Gensim and find similar words.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidate_assignment_rule: Cluster only. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across clusters. Prefer tight clusters; topic overlap alone is not a cluster.

web_access_policy.instruction: Do not use web search or open URLs. Use only the provided candidate cards.
